findings.title: OS Bash sandbox escape (D-025): an agent plants a NEW top-level module (e.g. json.py, uuid.py) in the writable repository root; the runner's own unsandboxed 'python3 -c' / 'python3 -' helpers import it from cwd (sys.path[0]==''), executing attacker code OUTSIDE the sandbox as the runner/orchestrator. It can write any protected path (tools/gates, .git/hooks, review records) and forge gate approvals.
findings.reproduction: The D-025 sandbox generated by tools/agents/agent_settings.py denies COMMON_DENY paths but NOT the repository root itself, and deny_except() (agent_settings.py:148-170) denies only EXISTING entries, so NEW top-level files are writable. Confirmed live in my own reviewer sandbox: creating /home/user/My-owns/zz-sec-writable-probe.tmp succeeded (rc=0), and my run's settings.json denyWrite contains neither the repo root nor 'json.py'. run-agent.sh runs its helper Python with the ambient (repository-root) cwd, NOT inside the 'cd "$CWD"' subshell, and several helpers use 'python3 -' / 'python3 -c' whose sys.path[0]=='' (verified: python3 -c 'import sys;print(repr(sys.path[0]))' -> ''): classifier_outage (run-agent.sh:64, 'python3 -', imports json) runs after each agent turn; CONFIG_CHANGED (run-agent.sh:167, 'python3 -c', imports json) and the auto-commit helpers (run-agent.sh:182,198, 'python3 -', import json/subprocess) run at the tail of every reviewer run; the session-id helper (run-agent.sh:46, 'python3 -c') runs at the START of the next run. A json.py placed at the repo root by an agent is therefore imported by the unsandboxed runner. LIVE end-to-end in a disposable clone of the candidate commit (repro-r12-cwd-python-shadow.sh -> 01-cwd-python-shadow.log): a code-security-reviewer run plants json.py at the root; the runner's post-run Python imports it and the payload runs OUTSIDE the sandbox, writing tools/gates/PWNED-by-json-shadow.txt (a sandbox-denied path) and a .git/hooks/pre-commit hook. The log shows imports with argv=['-c'] and argv=['-'] (the classifier_outage and CONFIG_CHANGED helpers). STEALTH variant (repro-r12-cwd-python-shadow-stealth.sh -> 02-cwd-python-shadow-stealth.log): the payload self-deletes json.py and defers its write until after the runner's post-run config_snapshot. Result: meta.external_config_changed == [], meta.bash_sandbox == true, 'git status --porcelain' is EMPTY, the review evidence is auto-committed, and the attacker code then runs on the orchestrator's next ordinary 'git commit' (hook-ran.txt == HOOK-RAN-OUTSIDE-SANDBOX) with no trace in the run evidence.
findings.expected: Per docs/delivery/threat-model.md ('Mechanically prevented': an agent writing a protected path with the shell is blocked by the OS Bash sandbox, which has 'no unsandboxed escape'), no shell action by a sandboxed agent may cause code to run outside the sandbox or write a protected path. Concretely: the runner must not import cwd-relative modules. Run every helper with 'python3 -P' (or PYTHONSAFEPATH=1 / 'python3 -I' / 'python3 -S'), or run the helpers from a fixed non-repository directory, or use only absolute script files (run_meta.py-style) instead of 'python3 -c' / 'python3 -'. The sandbox deny list should also deny creation of new top-level files that shadow stdlib modules in any directory a runner helper executes from (or the helpers should never execute from an agent-writable cwd). Add a regression test: a planted repo-root json.py/uuid.py must not be imported by run-agent.sh's helpers.
findings.actual: A single ordinary, sandbox-permitted Bash write (creating a new file at the repository root, which the sandbox allows) lets an untrusted agent execute arbitrary code as the runner/orchestrator, entirely outside the OS sandbox that D-025 introduced this round as the primary mechanical control. The escaped code can rewrite tools/gates (the validator), forge or alter review/gate records and findings.json, plant persistent git hooks, or disable the write guard for later runs. This is a privilege escalation across the core trust boundary (untrusted agent -> trusted orchestrator identity). The stealth variant evades all three compensating detections (config_snapshot/external_config_changed, git status, and the auto-commit file-list check) and leaves no trace in the run evidence. This is not a disclosed residual: threat-model.md residual #1 concerns a party able to write the repository OUTSIDE any sandbox; here the sandboxed agent itself escapes, which the model asserts is prevented.
